newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly higher in active trading on Tuesday on short-covering and fresh buying from speculative players, traders said.

"Copper found strong support at the key level of 20,000 yuan with speculative sellers seen offsetting their positions for quick profits after sharp falls over the past few trading days," said one trader.
"This triggered follow-through buying at that level," he said.
"But the short-term market trend is still uncertain as copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) has not shown signs of recovery," the trader added.
The most actively traded December 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 20,460 yuan ($2,468) per tonne, up 50 yuan.
It opened at 20,020 and hit a low of 19,980.
September rose 90 yuan to 20,290, October added 20 to 20,380, November gained 70 to 20,470 and the January 1998 contract 60 to 20,500. February was unchanged at 20,500.
Combined volume rose to 105,150 tonnes from 81,710.
Copper opened sharply lower on overnight losses on the LME but large volume short-covering and fresh buying pushed prices up from their lows to end near or at intraday highs.
On the LME, copper was again hit by liquidation, following on from last Friday, with prices dropping to near seven-month lows of $2,153 at one stage. Last kerb trade was at $2,162, down $51.
In Shanghai, physical copper prices are around the 20,300 yuan level, unchanged from Monday's close, traders said.
They said copper would fall again if the LME ends weaker tonight.
"A technical rebound is responsible for today's slight gains but copper will remain at low levels over the next few days," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended mostly higher. September rose 200 to 14,500 yuan per tonne, October gained 80 to 14,550. November was unchanged at 14,600 while December put on 40 to 14,600.
Combined volume fell to 890 tonnes from 4,280.
